'''Bruce Ronald Bowman''' (February 4, 1945 – December 31, 2020) was an American [[aerospace engineer]]. He was an [[astrodynamicist]] at the [[United States Air Force Space Command|U.S. Air Force Space Command]] from 2000 to 2013. He developed the [[Jacchia Reference Atmosphere|Jacchia-Bowman Density Model]], a [[reference atmosphere]] used widely for spacecraft [[orbit determination]] and [[atmospheric entry]] simulations.

==Early life and education==
Bowman was born in 1945.<ref name=":0" /> As a child, he saw [[Sputnik 1]] orbit overhead in 1957.<ref name=":1" /> He earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in astronomy from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1967.<ref name=":0" /> He later earned a [[Master of Science]] from the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]] in 1974, where he studied satellite [[geodesy]] and [[geophysics]].<ref name=":0" /> 

==Career==
After graduating, Bowman joined the [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] as a [[commissioned officer]], serving as a [[Captain (U.S. Air Force)|captain]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Bruce Bowman's Memorial |url=https://www.altogetherfuneral.com/obituaries/BruceBowman |website=Altogether |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref> He was a contractor in the federal civilian service for twenty years.

Bowman joined the [[Air Force Space Command]] as an astrodynamicist in 2000. He worked on the High Accuracy Satellite Density Model (HASDM) and associated [[satellite constellation]] used for calibration,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Storz |first1=Mark F. |last2=Bowman |first2=Bruce R. |last3=Branson |first3=Major James I. |last4=Casali |first4=Stephen J. |last5=Tobiska |first5=W. Kent |title=High accuracy satellite drag model (HASDM) |journal=Advances in Space Research |date=1 January 2005 |volume=36 |issue=12 |pages=2497–2505 |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2004.02.020 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0273117705002048 |access-date=20 March 2026 |issn=0273-1177|url-access=subscription }}</ref> serving until 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Space Weather Workshop 2007 {{!}} NOAA / NWS Space Weather Prediction Center |url=https://www.swpc.noaa.gov/content/space-weather-workshop-2007 |website=www.swpc.noaa.gov |publisher=National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Mentor Memorials |url=https://spacewx.com/mentor-memorials/ |access-date=20 March 2026 |publisher=Space Environment Technologies}}</ref> He was appointed a senior [[Research Scientist|research scientist]] at Space Environment Technologies, where he worked until 2020. He was a senior member of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA).

His research focused on the analysis of atmospheric [[Drag (physics)|drag]] on satellite orbits caused by [[Solar energy|solar heating]] and [[Solar storm|geomagnetic storms]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pilinski |first1=Marcin D. |last2=Argrow |first2=Brian M. |last3=Palo |first3=Scott E. |last4=Bowman |first4=Bruce R. |title=Semi-Empirical Satellite Accommodation Model for Spherical and Randomly Tumbling Objects |journal=Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets |date=May 2013 |volume=50 |issue=3 |pages=556–571 |doi=10.2514/1.A32348 |url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/1.A32348 |access-date=20 March 2026 |issn=0022-4650|url-access=subscription }}</ref> influenced by research from [[Luigi Giuseppe Jacchia]], Franco Verniani, and [[Charles E. Roberts (mathematician)|Charles E. Roberts]]. In 2006 and 2008, he published a revision of Jacchia's Reference Atmosphere called the Jacchia-Bowman Density Model (JB2008)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tobiska |first1=W. Kent |last2=Bouwer |first2=S. Dave |last3=Bowman |first3=Bruce R. |title=The Development of New Solar Indices for use in Thermospheric Density Modeling |journal=AIAA |url=https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20060052415 |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref> in which he parametrized important processes in the [[upper atmosphere]], including [[density]] variations, semiannual perturbations, and drag variations.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bowman |first1=Bruce |last2=Tobiska |first2=Barbara |last3=Marcos |first3=Frank |title=A New Empirical Thermospheric Density Model JB2006 Using New Solar Indices |journal=Aerospace Research Central |date=June 15, 2012 |doi=10.2514/6.2006-6166 |url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/6.2006-6166 |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bowman |first1=Bruce R. |title=A  New Orbital Analyst Tool for Associating Un-cataloged Analyst Debris  with Historical Launches, Breakups, and Anomalous Events |journal=Air Force Space Command |date=2011 |url=https://amostech.com/TechnicalPapers/2011/Orbital_Debris/BOWMAN.pdf |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref> The model is considered the most significant improvement on [[thermosphere]] density modeling since the 1970s. It is widely used for modeling [[Ballistic coefficient|ballistic coefficients]], improving collision avoidance, analyzing spacecraft [[accelerometer]] data, and simulating [[Orbital decay|orbit decay]] in transitional and [[free molecular flow]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Moe |first1=Kenneth |last2=Bowman |first2=Bruce R. |title=The Effects of Surface Composition and Treatment  On Drag Coefficients of Spherical Satellites |journal=American Astronautical Society |date=August 7, 2005 |url=https://spacewx.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/AAS_2005_258_Surface_Effects_on_CD_of_Spheres.pdf |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref>

The [[Committee on Space Research]] (COSPAR) adopted the Jacchia-Bowman model in the [[COSPAR International Reference Atmosphere]], and the [[International Organization for Standardization]] adopted the model as the standard for the upper atmosphere (IS 14222).<ref name=":0" /> The [[United States Space Command]] uses the model to propagate orbit predictions for every satellite in [[low Earth orbit]].<ref name=":0" />

He died in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] in 2020, aged 75.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
He married Esther Bowman in 1979. The couple resided in Colorado and had three children.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards ==
* Outstanding Senior Civilian Scientist Award, [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] (2007)<ref name=":1" />
* Rotary National Award for Space Achievement (2008)<ref name=":1" />
* Analyst Lifetime Achievement Award, [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] (2015)<ref name=":1" />
